report: The brain tissue section, stained with H&E, shows preserved architecture with no evident disruption. Notable are large neurons with prominent nucleoli and perinuclear halos, and smaller, dark-staining glial cells. Small, intact blood vessels contain red blood cells. No clear pathological changes are visible at this magnification without further clinical context.

evidence.title: Various antibody clones of Napsin A, TTF-1, and p40 in non-small cell lung carcinoma
evidence.text: This tissue-microarray study evaluated CK5, p63, and p40 as squamous markers and Napsin A and TTF-1 as lung adenocarcinoma markers. Reported performance varied by marker and antibody clone, and combining Napsin A with TTF-1 improved sensitivity.

evidence.title: Educational case: basal cell carcinoma and its histologic differential
evidence.text: Basal cell carcinoma shows dermal islands of basophilic tumor cells with peripheral nuclear palisading, stromal retraction, and loose mucinous stroma. Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma shows invasive islands of pleomorphic keratinocytes arising from the epidermis with prominent nucleoli and increased mitoses. Melanoma can show irregular nests and single pleomorphic pigmented melanocytes within the epidermis and dermis.

evidence.title: Colorectal carcinoma: pathologic aspects
evidence.text: Colorectal adenocarcinoma commonly forms malignant glands. Invasion can be accompanied by desmoplastic stroma, and glandular lumina frequently contain characteristic dirty necrosis. Benign colonic mucosa retains orderly crypt architecture and mature goblet cells without dysplasia.

evidence.title: Pulmonary adenocarcinoma histology
evidence.text: Pulmonary adenocarcinoma can show lepidic, acinar, papillary, micropapillary, or solid growth with mucin, and mixed patterns are common. Squamous differentiation is supported morphologically by keratinization, keratin pearl formation, and intercellular bridges. Poorly differentiated tumors may require immunohistochemistry.

evidence.title: Sampling and confirmation in infectious esophagitis
evidence.text: For suspected HSV esophagitis, diagnostic cytopathic changes are most likely at the ulcer edge and in sloughed squamous cells. Candida requires demonstration of pseudohyphae or true hyphae and assessment of tissue invasion rather than isolated budding yeasts in exudate. Histology may require organism-specific immunostaining, in situ hybridization, culture, or special stains for confirmation.

review.assessment: The vision models consistently predict 'lower-grade glioma', but the pathology report describes preserved brain architecture with no evident pathological changes, contradicting the criteria for glioma.
rationale: The de-identified report explicitly states 'preserved architecture with no evident disruption' and 'no clear pathological changes are visible', which contradicts the 'hypercellular glial proliferation' required for lower-grade glioma.
The report describes normal brain tissue components (large neurons with perinuclear halos, glial cells, intact blood vessels) rather than malignant features described in the candidate prompts.
discrepancies: Vision models (CONCH, MUSK, PLIP, QUILTNET) all classify the case as lower-grade glioma despite the pathology report indicating a lack of pathological changes.
recommended_review: Human pathologist review to reconcile the discrepancy between the 'no clear pathological changes' report and the model's glioma classification.
limitations: The retrieved literature provides morphology for lung, colorectal, and skin cancers, but no specific reference for lower-grade glioma morphology to contrast against the report.
